In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CS binding to Ni2+ and Cu2+ is normal for simple peptides without side-chains, and Im binding is the normal mode of binding to simple peptides with side-chains.
the choice between CS or Im binding is determined by the presence or absence of a side-chain Lewis-basic group.
CS binding is a common binding pattern for Ni(ii) and copper complexes of small peptides, but Im binding can be induced by deprotonation or side-chain Lewis-basic sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CS binding mode is the default binding mode for Ni(ii) and, to a lesser extent, Cu(ii) to peptides.

the CS binding mode is preferred for Ni(ii) and is the normal mode of binding for Cu(ii), but the Im binding mode can be accessed for both ions in the presence of a suitable side-chain Lewis basic site, or in the presence of an accessible deprotonation site.

the choice between CS or Im coordination patterns is not a simple function of the metal ion, but depends on the peptide ligand structure, and on the protonation and deprotonation states of both ligand and metal ion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metal ions in peptides are not necessarily Im-bound, and that the CS binding pattern is a viable alternative.
the choice between CS binding and Im binding is not a simple function of metal-ion size.
the choice of metal-ion binding mode is not as simple as one would expect from the simple electrostatic model of the alkaline earths.
